sources.note: All four personas ran. Screens 13 and 29 show the Android system "All files access" page; the tester judged them out of app, so their four marked elements carry no verdict and are listed under detection_false_positives. Persona complaints recorded in a session's out_of_scope list (including untested ones) are not counted as purpose issues.

screen1-a1.appearance: gold crown with a red jewel
screen1-a1.description: gold crown picture in the top bar, left of the gear

tester.deciding_evidence: no visible label in any state; the crown opened a paid subscription offer, which nothing on the screen announced
tester.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

personas.expectation: I think it opens something about paying for a premium version. A crown is not a function, it is an idea of 'royal' or 'best', so I am inferring 'premium' from it.
personas.cue: Only the picture of a gold crown. There is no text next to it.
personas.why: A crown does not depict an action. I have to translate a symbol into 'upgrade' or 'premium', and I could be wrong; it could also be an award, a ranking, or a profile badge.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Premium' or 'Upgrade' under or next to the crown, the way the Settings screen does with 'Upgrade to Premium'.

personas.expectation: I do not know. A crown might mean something special or something I would have to pay for, but that is a guess.
personas.cue: Only the picture of a crown. There is no word with it.
personas.why: A crown is not a symbol I know on a telephone. I would have to work out what it means, and whatever I worked out today I would not remember tomorrow, so I would not press it.
personas.solution: Put a plain word under or beside it, such as 'Upgrade' or 'Buy the full version', so I know before I press it.

personas.expectation: I think it would take me to a page asking me to pay for a premium version of the app.
personas.cue: Only the picture of a crown. There are no words on it.
personas.why: A crown is a picture, not a word, and I do not recognise pictures reliably. 'Crown means paid upgrade' is something I have to work out and hold in my head; nothing on this screen confirms it, so I stop and doubt it.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Premium' (or 'Upgrade') under the crown.

screen1-a1.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

screen1-a2.appearance: gear with a wrench laid across it
screen1-a2.description: gear with a wrench laid across it, top bar far right
screen1-a2.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a2.classification_basis: Gopal (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "The cog wheel looks something like the settings picture on my own telephone, but the spanner across it makes it a different picture from the one I know."; why "A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it."; solution "Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone."; after testing: "The cog led to a page plainly headed 'Settings', and 'Tools' led somewhere quite different. So pressing it is safe and the heading tells me where I am once I arrive. I still could not be sure before pressing, because the picture has a spanner added and no word, so it remains a small difficulty rather than none." | Kwame (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways."; why "The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it."; solution "Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'."; after testing: "The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it." — the cue names a picture that was there but could be read two ways (settings or tools); the fix asked is to plain the picture and word it

tester.deciding_evidence: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises

personas.expectation: Probably opens Settings. But the picture is a gear with a wrench through it, and the bottom bar also has an item called 'Tools', so it could also be tools or maintenance.
personas.cue: Only the gear-and-wrench picture. No text.
personas.why: A plain gear I would read as settings. A gear plus a wrench is two symbols combined, and 'wrench' literally means tools. With a 'Tools' tab on the same screen I cannot be sure which one this is.
personas.solution: Label it 'Settings' in text, or use a plain gear only, so it does not overlap with the 'Tools' tab.

personas.expectation: Probably the settings for this programme, where I change how it works.
personas.cue: The cog wheel looks something like the settings picture on my own telephone, but the spanner across it makes it a different picture from the one I know.
personas.why: A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it.
personas.solution: Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone.

personas.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.
personas.cue: Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways.
personas.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
personas.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

personas.expectation: Opens the app's settings.
personas.cue: The gear shape. But the spanner across it made me hesitate - there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so is this settings or tools?
personas.why: A gear on its own I'd read as settings instantly. The spanner on top makes it look like 'tools', and with a Tools tab at the bottom I honestly don't know which of the two holds which. I'd have to tap both to find out, which is exactly the kind of detour that loses me.
personas.solution: Either a plain gear, or a one-word label 'Settings' under it, so it can't be mixed up with the Tools tab.

screen1-a2.disagreement_note: tester: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises; Gopal: "A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it."; Kwame: "The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom."
screen1-a2.recommendation: Gopal: "Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone."; Kwame: "Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'."

screen1-a3.description: pill-shaped chip reading "PDF" in the file-type row under the title (drawn as the current/selected item; tapping the current item changes nothing but the item carries the selected state, so it stays in scope)

tester.deciding_evidence: the tap switched the selected file type to PDF, as the word on it predicts

screen1-a4.description: pill-shaped chip reading "HWP" in the file-type row under the title

tester.deciding_evidence: pressing it only recoloured the chip; neither the chip nor the result ever says what "HWP" is
tester.recommendation: spell out the format, e.g. "Hangul (HWP)" or "HWP documents", or drop the chip in locales where the format is not used

personas.expectation: I have no idea. Some other kind of file, perhaps.
personas.cue: Only the letters 'HWP', which mean nothing to me.
personas.why: 'HWP' is a set of initials I have never met. I cannot learn a new abbreviation and keep it, so this button is simply closed to me.
personas.solution: Spell it out in ordinary words, for example the full name of the kind of document it means, or leave it out if few people need it.

personas.expectation: I think it would show only files of the HWP type. I do not actually know what an HWP file is.
personas.cue: The word 'HWP', and that its neighbours are file types I know (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT).
personas.why: I can infer from the neighbours that it is a kind of document, but 'HWP' itself means nothing to me. I have to reason my way to it rather than simply read it.
personas.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

screen1-a4.recommendation: spell out the format, e.g. "Hangul (HWP)" or "HWP documents", or drop the chip in locales where the format is not used

screen1-a7.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback

No ordinary word appeared. I am still left guessing at initials." — the cue is the letters "PPT", which were there but unusable; the fix asked is to change the wording to an ordinary name

screen1-a8.description: small faint grey X at the top-left corner of the "Set as default reader" strip
screen1-a8.classification_basis: Yuki (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "A very small, very pale X in the top-left corner of the box. The book picture next to it looks like a logo, not a button."; why "The X is so tiny and faint I nearly missed it, and it's squashed together with a book picture that looks like decoration. I can't tell if tapping the box closes the strip or opens something. I really want this strip gone - it's an interruption - so I need the close to be obvious."; solution "A clear, normal-sized X (or 'Not now') at the right end of the strip, separate from the book picture."; after testing: "It does exactly what I hoped: the strip goes away and nothing else happens. So what it's for is fine. The problem left is that the x is tiny, pale and slow to respond. I nearly missed it, and I nearly pressed twice because nothing happened for a few seconds. That's more about size and faintness than purpose, but it still slowed me down." — after testing she says what it is for is fine; what remains is that the x is tiny, faint and slow — a visibility complaint, not a purpose one, so neither category fits

tester.deciding_evidence: the X dismissed the strip, exactly as the close convention promises

personas.expectation: I think the small 'x' closes this 'Set as default reader' strip. But the box also contains the book picture, which looks like a logo, and pressing a logo does something else, or nothing.
personas.cue: The tiny 'x' in the corner. An 'x' usually means close.
personas.why: The box contains two different things: a close mark and a book picture. I cannot tell whether I am pressing 'close' or pressing the book. The 'x' is also so small and faint that I almost did not see it.
personas.solution: Make the close button a separate, clearly visible 'x' (or the word 'Close' / 'Dismiss') at the right end of the strip, apart from the book picture.

personas.expectation: The small 'x' would probably close this grey strip. The red book I think is only a decoration.
personas.cue: A faint 'x' in the corner, which usually means close. But the box also holds the book picture, so I am not sure which part I am pressing.
personas.why: An 'x' for close is familiar to me, but this one is so faint and small I nearly missed it, and it is mixed up with a picture of a book that does not say what it does.
personas.solution: Make the 'x' clearly visible, or put the word 'Close' or 'No thanks' there, apart from the book picture.

personas.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.
personas.cue: A tiny, pale 'x' in the corner. It is so faint I almost missed it.
personas.why: The 'x' is the only cue and it is barely visible; the box also covers the book picture, which does not look like a close button at all. I cannot be certain what part I am meant to press or what will happen.
personas.solution: Make the close control a clearly visible 'x' of normal size, or a word such as 'Dismiss', on its own, away from the book picture.

personas.expectation: I think it closes (gets rid of) the 'Set as default reader' strip. But the box is mostly around the book picture, so it might open something about the reader instead.
personas.cue: A very small, very pale X in the top-left corner of the box. The book picture next to it looks like a logo, not a button.
personas.why: The X is so tiny and faint I nearly missed it, and it's squashed together with a book picture that looks like decoration. I can't tell if tapping the box closes the strip or opens something. I really want this strip gone - it's an interruption - so I need the close to be obvious.
personas.solution: A clear, normal-sized X (or 'Not now') at the right end of the strip, separate from the book picture.

screen1-a8.disagreement_note: tester: the X dismissed the strip, exactly as the close convention promises; Yuki: "The X is so tiny and faint I nearly missed it, and it's squashed together with a book picture that looks like decoration."
screen1-a8.recommendation: Yuki: "A clear, normal-sized X (or 'Not now') at the right end of the strip, separate from the book picture."

screen1-a11.appearance: white corner brackets with a horizontal line through the middle, on a black circle
screen1-a11.description: round black floating button with white corner brackets and a line through the middle

tester.deciding_evidence: the viewfinder glyph promised scanning but the tap produced an all-files permission request that never mentions scanning, so neither the glyph nor its result tells the user what the button does
tester.recommendation: give the button a visible label such as "Scan to PDF" (an extended floating button), and if file access is a prerequisite say so in the prompt ("To save scans, allow file access")

personas.expectation: Probably opens the camera to scan a paper document. The corner brackets look like a camera viewfinder frame. It could also be a QR-code scanner, or a 'select area' tool.
personas.cue: Only the four-corner-bracket picture. No text.
personas.why: Corner brackets are the shape of a frame, not of an action. Scan document, scan QR code and crop all use that shape. I would have to press it to find out.
personas.solution: Put 'Scan' text under or on the button, or make it a wide button that says 'Scan document'.

personas.expectation: I have no idea. Possibly something to do with the camera, but that is a guess from nothing.
personas.cue: Nothing - only four corner marks. There is no word.
personas.why: I do not recognise this picture at all. I would have to work out what it means, and I cannot hold on to that. I would leave it alone.
personas.solution: Put a word on it or under it - 'Scan a paper document', if that is what it does.

personas.expectation: I think it might open the camera to scan a paper document. That is a guess.
personas.cue: Only the picture. The corner brackets look like a camera viewfinder. There are no words.
personas.why: It is a picture-only button, and I do not recognise pictures easily. I am inferring 'scan' from the shape and could be wrong; it might be a QR-code reader or something else.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Scan' on or under the button.

personas.expectation: Opens the camera to scan something - probably scanning a paper document into a PDF, but it could be a QR code scanner.
personas.cue: The corner-bracket picture, which I know from scanning apps. No word on it.
personas.why: It's the biggest, boldest button on the page, so it's clearly important, but it has no word. Corner brackets mean both 'scan a document' and 'scan a QR code' in the apps I use, and I don't know which this is until I tap it.
personas.solution: Put a word on it - 'Scan' or 'Scan document' - it's the main button, it deserves a label.

screen1-a11.recommendation: give the button a visible label such as "Scan to PDF" (an extended floating button), and if file access is a prerequisite say so in the prompt ("To save scans, allow file access")

screen7-a2.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen7-a2.classification_basis: Gopal (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "The cog wheel looks something like the settings picture on my own telephone, but the spanner across it makes it a different picture from the one I know."; why "A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it."; solution "Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone."; after testing: "The cog led to a page plainly headed 'Settings', and 'Tools' led somewhere quite different. So pressing it is safe and the heading tells me where I am once I arrive. I still could not be sure before pressing, because the picture has a spanner added and no word, so it remains a small difficulty rather than none." | Kwame (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "Only the picture. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. personas.expectation: Probably opens Settings. But the picture is a gear with a wrench through it, and the bottom bar also has an item called 'Tools', so it could also be tools or maintenance.

personas.solution: Label it 'Settings' in text, or use a plain gear only, so it does not overlap with the 'Tools' tab.

personas.expectation: Probably the settings for this programme, where I change how it works.

personas.why: A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it.

personas.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.

personas.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
personas.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

personas.expectation: Opens the app's settings.
personas.cue: The gear shape; and I have now seen a Settings page with a back arrow, and I assume this is how you get there - but the spanner still says 'tools' to me and there is a Tools tab too.

personas.expectation: I think the small 'x' closes this 'Set as default reader' strip. But the box also contains the book picture, which looks like a logo, and pressing a logo does something else, or nothing.
personas.cue: The tiny 'x' in the corner. An 'x' usually means close.

personas.solution: Make the close button a separate, clearly visible 'x' (or the word 'Close' / 'Dismiss') at the right end of the strip, apart from the book picture.

personas.expectation: The small 'x' would probably close this grey strip. The red book I think is only a decoration.

personas.why: An 'x' for close is familiar to me, but this one is so faint and small I nearly missed it, and it is mixed up with a picture of a book that does not say what it does.
personas.solution: Make the 'x' clearly visible, or put the word 'Close' or 'No thanks' there, apart from the book picture.

personas.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.

personas.expectation: I think it closes (gets rid of) the 'Set as default reader' strip. But the box is mostly around the book picture, so it might open something about the reader instead.

personas.expectation: I think it opens something about paying for a premium version. A crown is not a function, it is an idea of 'royal' or 'best', so I am inferring 'premium' from it.

personas.expectation: I do not know. A crown might mean something special or something I would have to pay for, but that is a guess.

screen35-a2.appearance: gear with a wrench laid across it

So pressing it is safe and the heading tells me where I am once I arrive. I still could not be sure before pressing, because the picture has a spanner added and no word, so it remains a small difficulty rather than none." | Kwame (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways."; why "The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. personas.expectation: Probably the settings for this programme, where I change how it works.

The book and the x both just close the strip, and nothing else happens. The whole corner is one close target, so it does not matter which part I press. The x is still tiny and faint, but that is a visibility issue, not a question of what it does.
